name: scroll-island

frames.best_why: The ring is 88% filled and the island reads clearly against the article at the page end.

tagline: Floating pill tracks how far down the page you have scrolled.
summary: A slim dark island pinned to the top of a long article. A small ring fills as the reader scrolls and a percentage counts up; clicking it expands into a short list.
appearance: A small dark rounded pill sits centred near the top of a black article page, floating over the text. Inside it a thin circular ring on the left, a short title in the middle and a percentage on the right. The page behind is dense grey-white body copy.
behaviour: As the reader scrolls, the ring sweeps round and the percentage climbs from near zero toward a hundred. Clicking the pill springs it wider and taller to reveal the list passed in as children, then clicking again folds it back.
demo_content: An engineering blog post titled How we rebuilt sync for real-time teams, with the island label Rewriting sync.
search_phrases: circular progress ring pinned to top
sticky pill showing how far you read
reading progress bar for a blog
use_when: A long article, docs page or report where readers want to see how far through the page they are without a sidebar.
avoid_when: Fixed top centre, so it can cover headings on small screens, and it only reads window scroll, not an inner box.
customise: Set the title, pill height and className as props; the child list appears under the header when clicked. Widths, colours and the spring are fixed in the source.
weight_why: One fixed pill with a spring layout animation and a small SVG ring; idle when not scrolling.

a11y.note: The pill is a clickable div with no button role or tabindex, so it cannot be opened by keyboard; the progress ring has no progressbar role.

issues: The island is tiny against a full page of text, so the progress is easy to miss.
polish_why: Nice glass pill and spring; the demo makes it tiny against a wall of text.
title: Scroll Island
